subject: Data lifecycle question: which interaction elements are archived automatically?
messages:
From: Natalie James <natalie.james@brightbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: 2026-09-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick Q — what exactly gets archived by default?

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team had a follow-up on data lifecycle. Two quick things they want spelled out before procurement moves forward:

1) Which parts of an interaction are "archived" by default (e.g., raw user input, model prompts, intermediate token streams, final completions, session transcripts, KV cache snapshots)?
2) For anything retained by default, what are the default retention windows and how do we request erasure/proof of deletion?

We need a concise statement we can attach to the SOW. If you have a one-pager or matrix that maps element -> default retention -> residency/options, that would be perfect.

Best,
Natalie
Natalie James
Senior InfoSec Manager, BrightBank
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Natalie James <natalie.james@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what exactly gets archived by default?

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear ask. High level summary below, plus I'm attaching a short retention matrix (redwood-default-retention-summary.pdf) that you can include with the SOW.

TL;DR: by default we persist finalized request/response records (inputs + model outputs) for a limited retention window; ephemeral buffers and KV caches used for in-flight streaming are not archived by default.

What we archive by default (typical hosted API behavior):
- Finalized request record: user-provided request payloads that are marked as part of the request object (includes prompt text and metadata) — default retention: 180 days.
- Finalized model output(s): the model's completed outputs returned to the client (completions, chat replies) — default retention: 180 days.
- Session transcript (if explicitly requested via session recording flag): persisted as transcript artifacts — default retention: 365 days (customer can opt for shorter windows).
- Audit logs / system-level telemetry: operational logs used for billing/SRE (token counts, latency) — default retention: 7 years for audit/finance purposes (redacted where required).

What we do NOT archive by default:
- Streaming buffers and intermediate token fragments emitted during an active stream — these are held in-memory or short-lived buffers and are not written to durable storage by default (evicted after session close or 30 days in debugging mode).
- Inference KV cache snapshots: ephemeral model caches are not persisted as customer-visible artifacts and are not part of the archived record set, unless explicitly exported by the customer.
- Transient debug traces (full low-level binary traces) are only captured if a customer enables debugging and consents to storage; otherwise they are dropped.

Residency & erasure:
- Residency: archived artifacts are stored in the region you select at provisioning (us/eu/apac). We include KMS encryption for data at rest.
- Erasure: customers can request data deletion via the Console or API; standard deletion workflow includes a purge job and proof-of-deletion report (turnaround typically 48-72 hours for hosted customers).

I'll let Karthik add the technical nuances on streaming and debugging, but the attached matrix should give procurement what they need.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Product Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Natalie — adding a few technical clarifications to avoid ambiguity when you hand this to engineering/legal: 

1) "Finalized" means we persist the request and the completion that the service returned to the client after the model finished. If a client cancels mid-stream we do not persist the partial fragment as a finalized output unless the client explicitly instructs us to.

2) Streaming fragments are treated as ephemeral by default. For debugging pilots we offer an opt-in streaming capture mode (captured fragments are written to object storage for 30 days by default and require consent). If you rely on real-time stream replay for UX reasons, we recommend enabling an explicit capture flag and narrowing retention.

3) KV cache: we maintain an in-memory key-value cache per model instance to speed autoregressive decoding; we do not checkpoint these caches to durable blob storage in hosted mode. There is an export API for Dedicated/Private customers who want to snapshot a cache for warm-starting, and that export is treated as a customer artifact for retention/erasure purposes.

4) Attachments/embedded binary artifacts: if a request includes an uploaded file, the file is stored according to the same retention rules as the request object unless the customer requests separate handling.

5) Proof of deletion: we provide a deletion job id and a signed acknowledgement with timestamps. For EU/enterprise customers we can include a notarized deletion certificate as part of the compliance package (request via your CSM).

Happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk procurement through the matrix.

—Karthik

If procurement needs a PO-ready statement or a slightly shorter clause for the SOW, here's a drop-in sentence you can use: 

"Redwood will persist finalized request and response artifacts for the Customer's selected region under the default 180-day retention window for hosted accounts; streaming fragments, KV caches, and transient debug traces are ephemeral by default and are not archived unless the Customer explicitly enables capture. Redwood will execute deletion requests within 72 hours and provide auditable deletion receipts upon completion."

I'll send the attachments now; let me know if you need a redline or if legal wants the notarized deletion certificate included in the initial SOW.
